criteria.text: Cystic fibrosis homozygous for the F508del mutation in the CFTR gene.
Diagnosis of cystic fibrosis accompanied with results from a positive sweat test.
Homozygous F508del confirmed by FDA-cleared CF mutation testing, or prescriber documentation when lab results are unavailable.
Patient is at least 2 years old.
No concomitant strong CYP3A inducer, or dosage of the inducer adjusted to minimize the interaction.
No concomitant sensitive or narrow therapeutic index CYP3A substrate, or interacting medication dose adjusted or discontinued to minimize the interaction.

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Orkambi (lumacaftor/ivacaftor) Criteria Version 2; Last Updated 5/31/2016; Approval 4/19/2019; Effective 06/10/2019.

Encoded: closed CF homozygous F508del indication, CF diagnosis with positive sweat test results, mutation confirmation, age ≥2, and CYP3A inducer and substrate interaction requirements. Unknown or non-homozygous mutation status fails confirmation. The PDF typo F580del is normalized to F508del. Documentation verification requires manual review.

Reauthorization and duration (notes only): initial coverage up to 3 months. At treatment month 3, all initial criteria must still be met and prescriber follow-up by phone, email, or office visit must find no detriment or harm; approval may continue for 6 more months.

At treatment month 9, all initial criteria must still be met; submit documentation of no detriment or harm and slowed clinical decline/disease progression, clinical stabilization, or clinical improvement. Authorization may then be approved for 1 year. Renewal and duration require manual review.
Quantity limits (notes only): maximum 4 tablets/day (lumacaftor/ivacaftor 100/125 mg and 200/125 mg); maximum 2 packets/day (100/125 mg and 150/188 mg). Numeric quantity enforcement is not encoded.

Mechanism (notes only): lumacaftor improves F508del-CFTR conformational stability, processing and trafficking to the cell surface; ivacaftor potentiates CFTR channel opening to increase chloride transport. In vitro responses do not necessarily correspond to clinical benefit.
Kalydeco is linked as an alternative subject to its own indication and criteria.
